name: Top-down growth of artificial sea ice in 6.55 cm columns under a -5.1 C cryothermostat-cooled plate to quantify incorporation of particulate contaminants
plain_name: Freeze small columns of seawater to see how plastic particles get trapped in sea ice
description: Columns (6.55 cm diameter, 44 cm tall) of artificial seawater (31.28 g/L) on an orbital shaker in a 1 C room are frozen from the top for 19 h by an aluminium cooling element fed by a cryothermostat bath at -5.1 +/- 0.1 C; the ice is lifted out, centrifuged and some cores are kept at -20 C for micro-CT.
keywords: Freeze small columns of seawater to see how plastic particles get trapped in sea ice

sources.citation: Pradel et al. (2025) Impact of contaminant size and density on their incorporation into sea ice, Nature Communications

reported_equipment: cryothermostat bath with aluminium cooling elements

requirements.rationale: The circulating cryothermostat must hold the cooling element at -5.1 C (268.05 K).

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
